So Joy came back from the farmland in Moab with her daughter in law Ruth, the Moabite. And they got back to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. So there was a man who lived in Bethlehem whose name was Boaz and he was a member of Elimelech's family. And he was very powerful and influential and important and he was just a really honorable man. 

So one day, Ruth the Moabite went to her mother in law and she said, Would it be alright with you if I went to the field of some Kind hearted person and picked up the leftover grain after the harvesters have gone through and her mother in law said, yes, sure. Go ahead. So Ruth went out and she went into a field and she started picking up the leftover grain and it just so happened that this field belonged to Boaz, a Limelex relative. 

And then it just so happened that Boaz came out of Bethlehem and he came down to his field and he greeted his workers and said, Yahweh be with you. And his workers answered and said, Yahweh be good to you. And then he went up to the harvest supervisor and said, who is that woman over there? Who is her family? 

And the supervisor told him she's a moabite, the one who came back with joy from Moab. And she came up to me and she asked if she could gather up the grain from where the, they were leaving the bundles in the field. And she's been working ever since early morning until now. And she's only rested for a little bit in the shelter. 

So Boaz went up to Ruth, and he said, Listen, you don't need to go work in any other field. Just stay here in this one. See where the women are working over there? Just follow them. Work there. And I've already told the men there not to bother you. And if you get thirsty, you can just drink from the jugs that the men have filled up. 

And Ruth bowed down in front of him and said, sir, you're being so generous. You're treating me like I belong. And I'm an outsider. And Boaz said, look, I have already heard about everything you've done for your mother in law after your husband died, how you left your family and your homeland. And you came to a country where you didn't know anybody. 

May Israel's God, Yahweh, reward you and repay you for everything that you've done because you've put yourself under His protection. So Ruth said, "Thank you, sir, for being so generous. You've comforted me and put my mind at ease, and I'm not even going to become one of your servants."

# Bethlehem, Ephrathah

## Facts:

Bethlehem was a small city in the land of Israel, near the city of Jerusalem. It was also known as “Ephrathah,” which was probably its original name.

- Bethlehem has been called the “city of David,” since King David was born there.
- The prophet Micah said that the Messiah would come from “Bethlehem Ephrathah.”
- Fulfilling that prophecy, Jesus was born in Bethlehem, many years later.
- The name “Bethlehem” means “house of bread” or “house of food.”

(See also: Caleb, David, Micah)

## Bible References:

- Genesis 35:16
- John 7:42
- Matthew 2:6
- Matthew 2:16
- Ruth 1:2
- Ruth 1:21

## Examples from the Bible stories:

- **17:2** David was a shepherd from the town of **Bethlehem**.
- **21:9** The prophet Isaiah prophesied that the Messiah would be born from a virgin. The prophet Micah said that he would be born in the town of **Bethlehem**.
- **23:4** Joseph and Mary had to make a long journey from where they lived in Nazareth to **Bethlehem** because their ancestor was David whose hometown was **Bethlehem**.
- **23:6** “The Messiah, the Master, has been born in **Bethlehem**!”

## Word Data:

- Strong’s: H0376, H0672, H1035, G09650

So Boaz went up to the city gate, where people hung out and did business. And he sat down and waited. And it just so happened that along came that family guardian he'd been talking about, Mr. What's His Name. And so Boaz said, Hey, why don't you come and sit down here for a minute? So Mr. What's His Name came and sat down.

And then Boaz went and got ten elders and told them, Come and sit down over here. And so they did. So Boaz said to the family guardian, So you know that land that belonged to our relative Elimelech? Well, his widow Joy, who came back from Moab, is wanting to sell it. And I thought I would let you know about it in case you wanted to buy it and take responsibility for it.

And if you do, you could do that right now, right here in front of the elders and all these seated witnesses. But if you don't, just let me know because you're first in line and I'm next. And the family guardian said, Yes, I'll buy it. And Boaz told him, Okay. So, on the same day that you buy and take responsibility for the land from Joy and from Malon's widow, Ruth the Moabite, you also take on the responsibility to marry Ruth and have a son with her to carry on the family line. 

And then the family guardian said, Oh, oh no, I can't do that. That would mess up my inheritance. So you go ahead and buy the land and take over the responsibilities for the land and the family because I can't do it. So during that time in Israel, when people were discussing land transfers and the family guardianship responsibilities, when they wanted to make a deal official, one of them would take off his sandal and give it to the other one.

And that's what made everything official. So the family guardian told Boaz, You take over the responsibilities for the land and the family because I can't do it. And he took off his sandal. So then Boaz said to the elders and to all of the members of the extended family who were there, You all are witnesses today that I hereby buy and take responsibility for everything that belonged to Elimelech and to Melon and Kilion, which Joy currently has. 

And I also hereby agree to marry Ruth Madelon's widow to have a son with her to carry on the family line so that the land stays in the family and so that they don't lose their place in the family tree or their spot on the family council. You all are witnesses today and all the, the people there at the gate and the elders said, yes, we are witnesses. 

May Yahweh make this woman who's entering your house be like Rachel and like Leah, who together built up Israel's family, do what's right in the region of Africa. And maintain the family's reputation in the town of Bethlehem. And may the household that Yahweh gives you through the son that you have with this woman, may it be like the household of our ancestor Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah. 

So Boaz married Ruth, and they slept together, and Yahweh made it so that she got pregnant, and she had a baby boy. And all the women of the town told Joy, Isn't Yahweh just wonderful? He's given you a son to carry on the family line. He'll be a family guardian for you, and he'll preserve the family's reputation.

He'll give you back your life, and he'll take care of you when you're old. And he'll do all of this because he's the son of your daughter in law, and she loves you. And she is worth more than seven sons. So Joy picked up the baby, and she snuggled him, and she became a second mother to him. And all the women in Bethlehem spread the news everywhere that Joy had a son.

And the women named him Obed. Obed was the father of Jesse. And Jesse was the father of King David. This is the family tree of Perez. Perez had a son named Hezron. Hezron had a son named Ram. Ram had a son named Aminadab. Aminadab had a son named Nashun. Nashun had a son named Solomon. Solomon had a son named Boaz. 

Boaz had a son named Obed. Obed had a son named Jesse. And Jesse had a son named David.

So at mealtime, Boaz called Ruth over and was like, come over here, take some of this bread and dip it in that, in that sauce. And he got some roasted grain and gave that to her to eat too. And so she sat down next to his workers and ate and drank and. And she took the leftovers and saved them for later.

And then she went back to work. Then Boaz talked to his workers and he said, she's going to be gathering grain from between the bundles and you are not going to say anything at all to make her feel embarrassed about that. In fact, you are going to pull some of the grain out of the bundles and leave it there for her to gather.

And you will not do anything. To criticize her. So Ruth worked and she gathered up grain until it was evening. And then she took it and beat it to separate the kernels from the husks. And she gathered it all up and went back home to the city. And it was like 25 pounds of grain that she'd gathered. So she showed it to her mother in law and she also gave her the leftover food.

And her mother in law was like, Where did you work today? What happened? May whoever treated you so well receive good things in return. And so Ruth told her about everything that had happened and said, uh, the man's name was Boaz and her mother in law said, Oh, may Yahweh reward him because he hasn't forgotten his responsibilities to us who are alive or to our husbands who have died. 

This man is one of our closest relatives and that means he's one of our family guardians. And Ruth said, Oh, he also told me that I should stay with his workers for the whole harvest. And her mother in law said, Oh yes, that's good. Yes. Stay with the women who work for him. And that way you won't be bothered by any men in any other fields. 

So that's what Ruth did.
transcribing ruth 1 one to twenty one

\v23 So, Ruth stayed with the women who worked for Boaz. And she gathered grain in his fields for the entire barley harvest and the entire wheat harvest. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

[chapter division]

\v1 So, one day, her mother-in-law said to her, "My dear, it's time for me to find you a permanent home, someplace that's safe, secure, where you'll be provided for. \v2 You know Boaz, the man whose fields you've been working in? He's one of our closest relatives. And tonight, he and his men are working at separating the grain from the husks. \v3 So, here's what you're gonna do: Go take a bath, put on some perfume, put on your nicest clothes, and go down there to where they're working. But don't let Boaz see you until after he's finished eating and drinking. \v4 And then, when he goes to lie down, pay attention, so that you know where he is. Then, go and take the covers off of his legs, and lie down beside him. And he'll tell you what to do next."

\v5 So, Ruth told her mother-in-law, "Alright, I'll do it." \v6 And so, she went down to where Boaz and his men were at work, and she did everything that her mother-in-law said. \v7 So, Boaz ate, and he drank, and he was feeling pretty good. And so, then, he went down to the end of the barley pile and lay down go to sleep. And then, Ruth crept in, and she took Boaz' cloak from off of his legs, and she lay down beside him.

\v8 And then, about midnight, the man woke up all of a sudden, and he reached out his arm, and there was a woman right there! \v9 And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I'm Ruth, your woman. You are our family guardian, so put me under your protection." \v10 And he said, "May Yahweh reward you! Your family loyalty now is better than it was before, because you haven't gone chasing after any of the younger men in their prime, whether they're rich or poor. \v11 So, don't be afraid. I'm going to do everything that you've asked me to, because all of the decision-makers in our clan know that you are an honorable woman. \v12 But, even though I am a family guardian, there is another relative who's more closely related to you than I am. \v13 And so, he should be the one to take care of you. So, spend the night here, and tomorrow, if he agrees to do that, great. But if he doesn't, I promise that I will take care of you. So, spend the night here." \v14 And that's what Ruth did.

Then, early in the morning, she got up when it was still not light enough yet to recognize anybody. And Boaz was like, "Oo, we can't let anybody know that this woman came here tonight." \v15-16 And he told her, "Hold out your cloak." And so, she did. And he measured out six scoops of barley and put them on the cloak, and then bundled it up and put it on her shoulders. And she went back home to her mother-in-law, and he went into the city. So, when she got home, her mother-in-law said, "So, what happened?" And she told her everything that the man had said \v17 and she showed her the barley and said, "And he also gave me these six scoops of barley, because he was like, 'Don't go home to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'" \v18 And her mother-in-law said, "Ok! Now just sit and wait until we hear how this turns out, because this man isn't going to let it drop until it's all figured out today."

During the time when the tribal leaders were ruling Israel, there was a man named Elimelech, and he had a wife named Naomi, which means joy, and they had two sons named Melon and Kilion, and they lived in the town of Bethlehem in the region of Judah, and they were descended from one of the founding families of Bethlehem. 

Now, a famine hit the land, and there was no food, so Elimelech and his family moved to Moab, to the farmland there. And then Joy's husband, Elimelech, died, and she was left alone with her two sons. And after a while, the two sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah, and the other one named Ruth. And they lived there for about ten years.

And then the sons also died. And the poor woman, Joy, was left all alone, with no husband and no sons. Now, while she was there in Moab, she'd heard that Yahweh had provided for his people and that there was food again in Bethlehem. So she decided to go back home. So she set out from Moab back to Judah, and her two daughters in law came with her. 

And while they were there on the road back to Judah, Joy said to them, My dears, go back home to your mother's houses. May Yahweh be loyal to you, just like you've been loyal to me and to my sons. May He provide for you. Both of you go back and find new husbands, and may you find peace and security and rest in your husbands homes. 

And they all three embraced, and they hugged, and they all just wept like their hearts were broken. But Ruth and Orpah both said, No, no, we're going back with you. We're going back with you to your people. But Joy told them, No, my dears, why would you do that? Why would you go back with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?

No, I'm too old. I'm too old to get married and even if I could meet someone today and get married right away and get pregnant with sons tonight, would you really wait around for them to grow up so you could marry them? No. Why would you throw away your chances to be married? My life is just miserable, and it's so much worse than yours because Yahweh is working against me.

Go home. And the three of them hugged again and they wept, and Orpah kissed Joy goodbye and she went back. But Ruth threw her arms around her mother in law and wouldn't leave. And Joy said to her, Look, your sister in law has gone back to her people and to her gods. Just go with her. But Ruth said, No, I'm not going to leave you.

Stop trying to make me abandon you. I'm not going. Wherever you go, I'll go, and wherever you stay, I'll stay. Your people are my people, and your God is my God. Wherever you die, that's where I'll die, and where you're buried, that's where I'll be buried. And may Yahweh punish me in the most horrible way He wants to, if anything separates us, even after we're both dead. 

And so Joy noticed that her mind was made up, and so she stopped trying to persuade her to leave. And so the two of them went on together to Bethlehem. And when they got there, the whole town was just buzzing because of the two of them. And all the women were saying, Is it really Joy? Could it really be Joy? 

But Joy told them, Don't call me that. Why would you call me Naomi? Joy. Call me Mara. Misery. Because the All Powerful One has made my life miserable. When I left here, I had everything. And Yahweh has brought me back with nothing. Why would you call me Joy? Yahweh, the All Powerful One, has judged me and is punishing me.

# Almighty

## Facts:

The term “Almighty” literally means “all-powerful.” In the Bible, this term always refers to God.

- The titles “the Almighty” or “the Almighty One” refer to God and reveal that he has complete power and authority over everything.
- This term is also used to describe God in the titles “Almighty God” and “God Almighty” and “Lord Almighty” and “Lord God Almighty.”

## Translation Suggestions:

- This term could also be translated as “All-powerful” or “Completely Powerful One” or “God, who is completely powerful.”
- Ways to translate the phrase “Lord God Almighty” could include “God, the Powerful Ruler” or “Powerful Sovereign God” or “Mighty God who is Master over everything.”

(Translation suggestions: How to Translate Names)

(See also: God, lord, power)

## Bible References:

- Exodus 6:2-5
- Genesis 17:1
- Genesis 35:11-13
- Job 8:3
- Numbers 24:15-16
- Revelation 1:7-8
- Ruth 1:19-21

## Word Data:

- Strong’s: H7706, G38410
